extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent applicants, and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on when and how affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.131 ("swearing back") may be used to antedate references or overcome prior-art rejections, including what must be shown, form paragraphs to use, and who may sign. Focused on examination practice for patent prosecution and reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted use: Antedate a 35 U.S.C. 102(a) reference (less than 1 year)
rubrics_metrics.description: To antedate a reference or activity that qualifies as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) and not under 35 U.S.C. 102(b), e.g., where the prior art date under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) of the patent, the publication or activity used to reject the claim(s) is less than 1 year prior to applicant’s or patent owner’s effective filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the prior art reference under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) is a U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication, the reference may not be antedated if it claims the same patentable invention. See MPEP § 715.05 for “same patentable invention.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted use: Antedate a 35 U.S.C. 102(e) reference that shows but does not claim same invention
rubrics_metrics.description: To antedate a reference that qualifies as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(e), where the reference has a prior art date under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) prior to applicant’s effective filing date, and shows but does not claim the same patentable invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 715.05 for “same patentable invention.” See MPEP § 706.02(a) and § 2136–§ 2136.03 for explanation of what references qualify as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate use: Reference publication date more than 1 year prior (statutory bar under 35 U.S.C. 102(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 is not appropriate where the reference publication date is more than 1 year prior to applicant’s or patent owner’s effective filing date (a statutory bar under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a reference is a "statutory bar" under 35 U.S.C. 102(b) as referenced in 37 CFR 1.131(a)(2). A reference that only qualifies as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or (e) is not a "statutory bar."

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate use: Reference claims the same patentable invention (U.S. patent or application publication)
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 is not appropriate where the reference U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication claims the same patentable invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 715.05 for "same patentable invention" and MPEP Chapter 2300. Where reference patent and application/patent under reexamination are commonly owned and inventions are not patentably distinct, a terminal disclaimer and an affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.130 may be used to overcome a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103. See MPEP § 718.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate use: Foreign patent to same inventor filed >12 months before domestic (35 U.S.C. 102(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 is not appropriate where the reference is a foreign patent for the same invention to applicant (or legal representatives/assigns) issued prior to the filing date of the domestic application on an application filed more than 12 months prior to the filing date of the domestic application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate use: Reference should not have been used because applicant's parent application or Convention date is earlier
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 is unnecessary where the effective filing date of applicant’s or patent owner’s parent application or an International Convention-proved filing date is prior to the effective date of the reference, because the reference should not have been used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate use: Prior U.S. patent to same entity claiming same invention (double patenting)
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 is not appropriate where the reference is a prior U.S. patent to the same entity claiming the same invention; the question is one of double patenting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate use: Disclosure of prior U.S. patent to same party, not copending (dedication concern)
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 is not appropriate where the reference is the disclosure of a prior U.S. patent to the same party, not copending; the question is one of dedication to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note In re Gibbs, which substantially limited the doctrine of dedication. See cited case law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate use: Applicant has clearly admitted on the record that the subject matter is prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 cannot be used where applicant has clearly admitted on the record that subject matter relied on in the reference is prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited cases: In re Hellsund; In re Garfinkel; In re Blout; In re Lopresti. Such admissions bar overcoming the rejection by 1.131.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate use: Subject matter is prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(f)
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 is not appropriate where the subject matter relied upon is prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate use: Subject matter available under 35 U.S.C. 102(g)
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 cannot be used to overcome a reference when the subject matter relied on in the reference is prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.131 is designed to rebut presumptions of dates for references under 102(a) and 102(e), but 102(g) by definition requires the subject matter to have been made before applicant's invention. Cited case: In re Bass.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate use: Subject matter corresponds to a lost count in an interference (interference estoppel)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the subject matter corresponding to a lost count in an interference is prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(g) or barred to applicant by interference estoppel, 37 CFR 1.131 cannot be used to overcome the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited cases: In re Bandel; In re Kroekel; In re Deckler; In re McKellin; In re Zletz (where showing not "substantially the same" may allow 1.131). See MPEP § 2138.01 and § 2138.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference date to be overcome is the effective date of the reference
rubrics_metrics.description: The date to be overcome under 37 CFR 1.131 is the effective date of the reference (i.e., the date on which the reference is available as prior art).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should determine the effective date per categories (U.S. patents/publications, foreign patents, printed publications, activities) using MPEP references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date rule: U.S. patents, U.S. patent application publications, and international application publications
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. patents, U.S. patent application publications, and WIPO publications of international applications are available as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) against all patent applications and patents under reexamination; the effective date of a domestic patent when used as a reference is the effective U.S. filing date, not the foreign filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When entitled to claim benefit of an earlier filed application, effective filing date is determined under 35 U.S.C. 102(e). See MPEP § 706.02(a), § 706.02(f)(1), § 2136–§ 2136.03. Note: effective date of domestic patent is not the foreign filing date (In re Hilmer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date rule: Foreign patents
rubrics_metrics.description: For foreign patents, see MPEP § 2126–§ 2127 regarding date of availability of foreign patents as prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date rule: Printed publications
rubrics_metrics.description: A printed publication, including a published foreign patent application, is effective as of its publication date, not its date of receipt by the publisher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2128 through § 2128.02 for additional information regarding effective dates of printed publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date rule: Activities
rubrics_metrics.description: For activities (use/knowledge by others, admissions, or examiner's personal knowledge), the effective date of the activity used to reject the claim(s) is the date the activity was first known to have occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.57: Affidavit or Declaration Under 37 CFR 1.131: Ineffective - Heading
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶ 7.57  The [1] filed on [2] under 37 CFR 1.131 has been considered but is ineffective to overcome the [3] reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: bracket 1 insert --affidavit-- or --declaration--; must be followed by one or more of form paragraphs 7.58–7.63 or a paragraph setting forth proper basis for insufficiency (e.g., failure to establish acts performed in this country, or scope not commensurate with scope of claims).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.58: Ineffective — Claiming Same Invention
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶ 7.58  The [1] reference is a U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication of a pending or patented application that claims the rejected invention. An affidavit or declaration is inappropriate under 37 CFR 1.131(a) when the reference is claiming the same patentable invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reference and this application are not commonly owned, the reference can only be overcome by establishing priority through interference. If commonly owned, the reference may be disqualified by affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.130. If used to respond to submission under 1.131, paragraph must be preceded by 7.57. May be used without 7.57 to notify applicant that submission of 1.131 would be inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.59: Ineffective — Insufficient Evidence of Reduction to Practice Before Reference Date
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶ 7.59  The evidence submitted is insufficient to establish a reduction to practice of the invention in this country or a NAFTA or WTO member country prior to the effective date of the [1] reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.57. Examiner should provide explanation of lack of showing of the alleged reduction to practice in bracket 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.60: Ineffective — Reference Is a Statutory Bar
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶ 7.60  The [1] reference is a statutory bar under 35 U.S.C. 102(b) and thus cannot be overcome by an affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.57.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.61: Ineffective — Insufficient Evidence of Conception
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶ 7.61  The evidence submitted is insufficient to establish a conception of the invention prior to the effective date of the [1] reference. Conception must be capable of proof (demonstrative evidence or complete disclosure to another); more than a vague idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.57. Explanation of deficiency in showing of conception must be presented. If affidavit also fails to establish diligence or subsequent reduction to practice, follow with 7.62 and/or 7.63. If either diligence or reduction to practice is established, state that following this paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.62: Ineffective — Diligence Lacking
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶ 7.62  The evidence submitted is insufficient to establish diligence from a date prior to the date of reduction to practice of the [1] reference to either a constructive reduction to practice or an actual reduction to practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.57. If affidavit additionally fails to establish conception, 7.61 must also precede. If affidavit establishes conception, add a statement to that effect. Provide explanation for non-diligence in bracket 2. See MPEP § 715.07(a) regarding diligence not required after reduction to practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.63: Ineffective — Insufficient Evidence of Actual Reduction to Practice
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶ 7.63  The evidence submitted is insufficient to establish applicant’s alleged actual reduction to practice of the invention in this country or a NAFTA or WTO member country after the effective date of the [1] reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.57. If alleged reduction to practice is prior to effective date of reference, do not use this paragraph (use 7.59). If affidavit additionally fails to establish conception or diligence, 7.61 and/or 7.62 should precede. An explanation of lack of showing must be given in bracket 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.64: Effective To Overcome Reference
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶ 7.64  The [1] filed on [2] under 37 CFR 1.131 is sufficient to overcome the [3] reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 1 insert either --affidavit-- or --declaration--; bracket 2 insert filing date of affidavit/declaration; bracket 3 insert name of the reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.131 versus 37 CFR 1.132: Purpose and when to use 1.132
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of a 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit/declaration is to overcome a prior art rejection by proving invention of the claimed subject matter by applicant prior to the effective date of the reference or activity relied upon. Affidavits under 1.132 are used to show that the reference discloses applicant’s own invention (derivation/ownership issues).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits submitted improperly under 1.131 to show applicant's own invention will be considered as though filed under 1.132. Where reference relied upon in a 35 U.S.C. 103 rejection qualifies as prior art under 102(f) or (in certain cases) 102(e) for applications filed on/after Nov 29, 1999, applicant may overcome rejection by proving common ownership or common assignment at the time the later invention was made (see MPEP § 706.02(l)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Jointly-filed reference (applicant + another): 1.131/1.132 interplay
rubrics_metrics.description: When subject matter disclosed but not claimed in a patent or application publication filed jointly by S and another is claimed in a later application filed by S, the joint patent/publication is a valid reference under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or (e) unless overcome by affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 or an unequivocal declaration under 37 CFR 1.132 by S that he/she conceived or invented the subject matter disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclaimer by the other patentee/applicant should not be required but may be accepted. See In re DeBaun and MPEP § 716.10. Affidavits under 1.131 intended to show applicant’s own invention should be treated as though filed under 1.132.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common assignee rule: common ownership does not alone avoid 1.131 requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The mere fact that the reference patent or application publication and the application which claims it are owned by the same assignee does not avoid the necessity of filing an affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131, absent a showing under 37 CFR 1.132 that the patentee derived the subject matter from the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, for rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102(f)/103 or 102(g)/103 (or 102(e)/103 for certain post-1999 cases), a showing that the invention was commonly owned or subject to obligation of assignment to the same person at the time the later invention was made would preclude such rejection or be sufficient to overcome it. See MPEP § 706.02(l).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of applicant's own invention: overcoming publication references
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless it is a statutory bar, a rejection based on a publication may be overcome by showing it was published either by applicant himself/herself or on his/her behalf; when applicant is a co-author, applicant may overcome by filing 1.131 or 1.132 affidavit/declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When showing applicant's own invention under 1.131/1.132, the limitation in 35 U.S.C. 104 and in 37 CFR 1.131(a)(1) that only acts occurring in this country or NAFTA/WTO member countries may be relied on to establish a date of invention is not applicable for demonstrating the publication is applicant's own work. See MPEP § 716.10 and cited cases (Ex parte Lemieux; Ex parte Powell; In re Katz).

rubrics_metrics.name: Activities applied against the claims: how to overcome
rubrics_metrics.description: A rejection based on an activity showing the claimed invention was used or known prior to the filing date may be overcome by an affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 establishing a date of invention prior to the activity date, or by a specific affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.132 showing the activity was performed by the applicant(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: How much of the claimed invention must be shown (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit/declaration must establish possession of either the whole invention claimed or something falling within the claim (such as a species of a claimed genus), in the sense that the claim as a whole reads on it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit not insufficient merely because it does not show identical disclosure; must contain facts showing completion of the invention commensurate with the extent of the invention as claimed. If differences between claimed invention and affidavit showing are so small as to render claims obvious, an affidavit may need to show no more than the reference shows. See cited cases (In re Tanczyn; In re Stryker; In re Wakefield; In re Spiller).

rubrics_metrics.name: Swearing behind one of plurality of combined references
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may overcome a 35 U.S.C. 103 rejection based on a combination of references by showing completion of the invention by applicant prior to the effective date of any of the references; applicant need not antedate the reference with the earliest filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, the 1.131 affidavit must show possession of the whole invention as claimed or something within the claims prior to the effective date of the reference being antedated; it is not enough to show only what one reference happens to show if that reference does not itself teach the basic inventive concept. If claim rejected under 103 based on Reference A in view of Reference B, applicant can rely on teachings of Reference B to show differences would have been obvious prior to date of Reference A, but still must establish possession of claimed invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: General rule as to generic claims: single species may antedate genus (most cases)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference or activity applied against generic claims may (in most cases) be antedated as to such claims by an affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 showing completion of the invention of only a single species within the genus prior to the effective date of the reference or activity (assuming reference/activity is not a statutory bar or a patent claiming the same invention).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Ex parte Biesecker and cases; see exceptions for unpredictable arts — special practice in MPEP § 715.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genus-species practice where predictability is in question
rubrics_metrics.description: Where predictability is in question, the 1.131 affidavit/declaration must show as much as the minimum disclosure required by a patent specification to furnish support for a generic claim; showing one species may not ordinarily withdraw rejection if reference discloses another species not antedated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test: whether facts in the affidavit would persuade one skilled in the art that the applicant possessed enough of the invention to justify the claimed genus. In unpredictable arts, prior completion of one or a few species is generally not sufficient; number required depends on size and predictability of genus (e.g., small genus like halogens may require 2–3 species, large genus many). Cited cases: In re Shokal, In re Mantell, In re Rainer, In re DeFano, In re Clarke, In re Schaub.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference discloses species: species vs genus claim remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: If reference/activity discloses the claimed species, the rejection can be overcome directly by showing prior completion of the claimed species or indirectly by showing prior completion of a different species plus that the claimed species would have been an obvious modification of the applicant's species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reference discloses multiple species of a claimed genus, applicant must show prior completion of all species to directly overcome; indirect antedating possible via obviousness in view of applicant's species (cases cited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference discloses claimed genus: single species may suffice (unless unpredictability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the reference or activity discloses the claimed genus, a showing of completion of a single species within the genus is generally sufficient to antedate the reference or activity under 37 CFR 1.131.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In unpredictable arts, showing one or a few species is generally not sufficient; the test is whether species completed by applicant provided adequate basis for inferring generic applicability. See cited cases and examples regarding numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species versus embodiments: different treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: References or activities which disclose one or more embodiments of a single claimed invention (as opposed to species of a claimed genus) can be overcome by filing a 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit showing prior completion of a single embodiment of the invention, whether same or different embodiment from that disclosed in the reference/activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited cases: In re Fong, In re Defano.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may make affidavit or declaration: inventors and others
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties who may make an affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131: (A) All the inventors of the subject matter claimed; (B) Less than all named inventors where it is shown that less than all invented the subject matter of the rejected claim(s); (C) Where petition under 37 CFR 1.47 was granted or application accepted under 1.42/1.43, the 1.47 applicant or legal representative may sign; (D) The assignee or other party in interest when it is not possible to produce the affidavit/declaration of the inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: one of two joint inventors is accepted where shown sole inventor of the claim under rejection. See Ex parte Foster and cited MPEP sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formality note: Form paragraphs 7.57–7.64 available to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraphs 7.57–7.64 may be used by examiners to respond to 37 CFR 1.131 affidavits, ranging from headings indicating ineffectiveness to a paragraph indicating the affidavit is sufficient to overcome the reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each form paragraph has required precedents and bracketed insertions (e.g., filing date, reference name) and must be used per the Examiner Notes accompanying each paragraph.
